arxiv-2101-00445.title: Long Plane Trees Thanks: A preliminary version appeared as S. Cabello, M. Hoffmann, K. Klost, W. Mulzer, and J. Tkadlec. Long Plane Trees in Proc. 38th SoCG, pp. 23:1–-23:17.
arxiv-2101-00445.creator: Sergio Cabello, Michael Hoffmann, Katharina Klost, Wolfgang Mulzer, Josef Tkadlec
arxiv-2101-00445.description: Abstract In the longest plane spanning tree problem, we are given a finite planar point set 𝒫 \mathcal{P} , and our task is to find a plane (i.e., noncrossing) spanning tree for 𝒫 \mathcal{P} with maximum total Euclidean edge length. Despite more than two decades of research, it remains open whether this problem is NP-hard.

arxiv-2107-03309.title: Dynamical Fractional and Multifractal Fields
arxiv-2107-03309.creator: Gabriel B. Apolinário, Laurent Chevillard, Jean-Christophe Mourrat
arxiv-2107-03309.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Gabriel B. Apolinário, Laurent Chevillard, Jean-Christophe Mourrat. Motivated by the modeling of three-dimensional fluid turbulence, we define and study a class of stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs) that are randomly stirred by a spatially smooth and uncorrelated in time forcing term.

arxiv-2311-12964.title: Magnetointerferometry of multiterminal Josephson junctions Thanks: Institute of Melin2019 Univ. Grenoble Alpes Thanks: Institute of Melin2019 Univ. Grenoble Alpes
arxiv-2311-12964.creator: Régis Mélin, Clemens B. Winkelmann, Romain Danneau
arxiv-2311-12964.description: Abstract We report a theoretical study of multiterminal Josephson junctions under the influence of a magnetic field B B . We consider a ballistic rectangular two-dimensional metal N 0 N_{0} connected by the edges to the left, right, top and bottom superconductors S L S_{L} , S R S_{R} , S T S_{T} and S B S_{B} , respectively.

arxiv-2503-10529.title: PiSA: A Self-Augmented Data Engine and Training Strategy for 3D Understanding with Large Models
arxiv-2503-10529.creator: Zilu Guo, Hongbin Lin, Zhihao Yuan, Chaoda Zheng, Pengshuo Qiu, Dongzhi Jiang, Renrui Zhang, Chun-Mei Feng, Zhen Li
arxiv-2503-10529.description: Abstract 3D Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have recently made substantial advancements. However, their potential remains untapped, primarily due to the limited quantity and suboptimal quality of 3D datasets. Current approaches attempt to transfer knowledge from 2D MLLMs to expand 3D instruction data, but still face modality and domain gaps.

arxiv-2601-20224.title: Feature Projection Learning for Better Vision-Language Reasoning
arxiv-2601-20224.creator: Yi Zhang, Weicheng Lin, Liang-Jie Zhang \sthanks Corresponding author
arxiv-2601-20224.description: Abstract Vision-Language Pre-Trained models, notably CLIP, that utilize contrastive learning have proven highly adept at extracting generalizable visual features. To inherit the well-learned knowledge of VLP models for downstream tasks, several approaches aim to adapt them efficiently with limited supervision.

pmc-10542677.title: A mixed-method survey to understand the role of dog welfare organisations in Ireland, including reported challenges and potential solutions
pmc-10542677.creator: Claire McKernan, Catherine Lawler, Blain Murphy, Daniel M. Collins, Simon J. More, Sean Murray, Patricia Reilly, Rob Doyle, Natascha V. Meunier, Aiden Maguire, Locksley L. McV. Messam
pmc-10542677.description: BackgroundThis novel study forms part of a larger research programme seeking an improved understanding of aspects of the owned dog population in Ireland. Dog welfare organisations (DWOs) in Ireland are recognised as an instrumental pillar of the animal welfare sector with some receiving substantial public funding.

pmc-11534794.title: Gender differences in operational and cognitive abilities
pmc-11534794.creator: Emil Lager, Kimmo Sorjonen, Marika Melin
pmc-11534794.description: IntroductionGender differences in cognitive and operational abilities have been identified. Yet, their interrelationship remains underexplored. This prevents tailored evidence-based selection, allowing discrimination to persist.MethodsData from a test battery of operational and cognitive tests was analyzed. In total 2,743 aviation pilot candidates’ test scores were analyzed.

pmc-12457951.title: The Interplay Between Picky Eating, Other Eating Behaviors, and Obesity Indicators in Preschool Children
pmc-12457951.creator: Melika Mahmoudizadeh, Mina Babashahi, Milad Rajabzadeh‐Dehkordi, Mehran Nouri, Shiva Faghih
pmc-12457951.description: Picky eating (PE) during early childhood strongly affects children's food preferences. This research aimed to assess the association of eating behaviors with obesity indices among preschoolers. Our cross‐sectional analysis included 436 pre‐school children. For data collection, parents were interviewed face‐to‐face, using the Child Eating Behavior Questionnaire and the Food Frequency Questionnaire for children eating behaviors and dietary intakes, respectively.

pmc-12625453.title: Social support and its related factors among elderly people: a cross-sectional analysis within the PERSIAN Guilan Cohort Study (PGCS)
pmc-12625453.creator: Zahra Ahmadnia, Saman Maroufizadeh, Fateme Sheida, Masoud Faghih Akhlaghi, Fariborz Mansour-Ghanaei, Farahnaz Joukar
pmc-12625453.description: BackgroundThe worldwide rise in life expectancy has resulted in an expanding elderly population, particularly in developing nations, amplifying the demand for social support to manage the challenges associated with aging. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate social support and its associated factors among older adults in the Prospective Epidemiological Research Studies in Iran (PERSIAN) Guilan Cohort study (PGCS) population.

pmc-12720471.title: Global, regional, and national epidemiology of cervical cancer in elderly women from 1990 to 2021 and its prediction to 2035
pmc-12720471.creator: Yu Li, Kangtai Zheng, Qin Xu, Lingling Xie, Huaiwu Lu
pmc-12720471.description: BackgroundCervical cancer among elderly women poses a significant challenge to the elimination of cervical cancer. This study estimated the burden, trends, and disparities of cervical cancer in women aged ≥ 60 years from 1990 to 2021, with projections extending to 2035 at global, regional, and national levels.

pmc-13114383.title: Multistructural and Multiscale Instability Characterization of Gas–Liquid Two-Phase Flow with MRA-CMESSE
pmc-13114383.creator: Qing-Ming Sun, Qing-Chao Yu, Di Ba
pmc-13114383.description: Characterizing instability in gas–liquid flows is difficult because flow dynamics interact across multiple scales. In this work, we develop an integrated framework that combines multi-resolution analysis with composite multiscale equiprobable symbolic sample entropy (MRA-CMESSE). This combination enables us to examine flow instability from a multistructural and multiscale perspective.
